title: Why popcorn pops
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why do some kernels not pop?
What temperature does popcorn pop at?

explain.say: Each popcorn kernel has a hard, watertight shell called the hull, packed with starch and a little water, about 14 percent.
As the kernel heats past 100 degrees Celsius, the water turns to steam. The tough hull traps it, so the pressure inside climbs faster and faster.
The hot steam also softens the starch into a gooey gel. At around 180 degrees, the pressure is about nine times normal air pressure, and the hull bursts.
The steam rushes out and the soft starch puffs into a white foam, which sets as it cools. That fluffy foam is the popcorn you eat.

faq.a: Water inside the kernel turns to steam, but the tough hull traps it. The pressure rises until the hull suddenly bursts.

faq.q: Why do some kernels not pop?
faq.a: Their hulls may be cracked and leak steam, or they may have dried out and have too little water inside to build enough pressure.

faq.q: Why does popcorn turn into white fluff?
faq.a: Hot steam turns the starch into a soft gel. When the hull bursts, the gel puffs up into a foam full of bubbles, which hardens as it cools.
asks: What is the white part of popcorn?

faq.a: Most other corn has a thinner, leakier hull, so steam escapes slowly and pressure never builds up enough to burst it.
Scientists filming popcorn found the pop comes from the burst of steam rushing out as the hull breaks.

facts: A popcorn kernel bursts at about 180 degrees Celsius, when the steam inside reaches roughly nine times normal air pressure.
Popcorn kernels need about 14 percent water inside to pop well.
